title: Geillis Glasgow, spouse of Thomas Wilson at Chaplehill: testament dative, 1603

plain_english: Geillis Glasgow is expressly described as the spouse of Thomas Wilson at Chaplehill in Ardrossan parish. She died intestate in January 1603.

Thomas supplied the testament in the name and on behalf of a group that includes James, Isobel and Bessie Wilson. The obscured words between the names and the appointment prevent a safe statement of their family relationships.
The executor appointment is tied to a commissary decree on the last day of April 1603. The estate was confirmed at Glasgow on 11 May 1603.
The inventory is agricultural: it includes cattle, sheep, grain/crops and household furnishings. Several quantities and valuations remain unresolved.

The record says no debts were owed to the estate, then lists debts owed by it. Those include rent or ferm to the lord of Eglinton, an amount to James Glasgow in Stevenston, and past wages to Robert Boyd and a servant named Bessie whose surname is unclear.
James Glasgow is a creditor or payee in the debt section. The testament does not call him Geillis's father, brother or other relative.
findings: Explicit spouse and locality: Geillis Glasgow was spouse of Thomas Wilson at Chaplehill, in Ardrossan parish.
Explicit timing: death in January 1603; executor decree 30 April 1603; confirmation 11 May 1603.

James, Isobel and Bessie Wilson are named in the executor passage, but the relationship words are not securely legible. Executor status is an administrative role and does not itself prove that they were children.
James Glasgow in Stevenston occurs in the debts owed by the estate. This is financial network evidence only; no kin term accompanies his name.
Robert Boyd and a servant Bessie are owed for past service. The servant Bessie must not be assumed to be the Bessie Wilson in the executor passage.
The estate appears debt-heavy: the clerk explicitly writes that debts exceed goods after listing no debts owing to the estate.
changes_from_previous: Fresh visual inspection of both originals preceded comparison with the saved profile findings and index assessments.
The earlier summary's core spouse, locality and January death reading is supported directly by the manuscript.
The executor clause remains less certain than a prior reading of James Wilson as a lawful son: the obscured intervening words do not support restoring confident sonship.
The manuscript supplies two distinct administrative dates: the last day of April for the decree appointing executors and 11 May 1603 for confirmation.
James Glasgow is visibly embedded in the debts-awand section, reinforcing that his occurrence is financial, not an express kinship statement.
unresolved: The exact words between James Wilson and Isobel/Bessie Wilson in the executor clause, and therefore the precise relationships among the named Wilsons.
Complete item-by-item reading of livestock/crop quantities, valuations and the final account totals.
The surname of the servant Bessie and whether she is distinct from every other Bessie named in the entry.
The identity and kinship, if any, of James Glasgow in Stevenston; this testament alone does not resolve him to a profile.
Geillis's parentage and any proposed sisterhood with Katherine Glasgow remain external hypotheses, not statements in this record.
profiles: Geillis Glasgow/Wilson: maintained profile association; spouse, locality and death month are direct
James Wilson: named in the executor passage; possible son remains uncertain because the relationship words are unresolved
confidence_statement: High for Geillis Glasgow's name, Thomas Wilson as spouse, Chaplehill in Ardrossan parish, January 1603 death, the April decree and 11 May confirmation. High that James Glasgow in Stevenston appears in the debt section and no kin term is visible there. Moderate for the named executor group; low for the words defining their relationships and for many financial figures. This is a complete working reading of the supplied entry, with unresolved text shown rather than silently reconstructed.
